articleTitle: Hybrid CNN-Total Variation Deconvolution for Mitigating Atmospheric Seeing Effects in Ground-Based Astronomical Imaging
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Advances in Computing and Communications (ICACC)
abstract: Ground-based telescopes often suffer from atmospheric seeing effects, which degrade the quality of astronomical images that are acquired. In this paper, we present an innovative hybrid model of Total Variation Deconvolution (TVD) and Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) architecture to tackle this challenge. The developed model was designed in the order of TVD as the first layer, three other layers of CNN followed, which created a four-layer structure. This is a strength-based model of both TVD and CNN, with the objective of image deblurring, clearness, sharpness, and fine detail preservation in the image. Performance measures of our hybrid model were evaluated using Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR) and Structural Similarity Index (SSIM) metrics along with visual inspection. The results show that the hybrid approach will significantly improve image quality over traditional methods, presenting a promising solution in improving resolution and detail in ground-based astronomical observations.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-Based Identification of Pneumonia in Chest X-Ray Images
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Advances in Computing and Communications (ICACC)
abstract: Pneumonia is a serious infection caused by bacteria, viruses, or fungi invading the lungs. This leads to inflammation of the alveoli, causing them to fill with fluid, which can result in symptoms such as coughing, difficulty breathing, or chest pain. Addressing the growing demand for AI-driven diagnostic tools in healthcare, particularly for pneumonia detection, this work presents an effective approach using deep learning techniques.Training models to differentiate between pneumonic and normal chest X-ray pictures is the main goal of the project. To evaluate the patient’s health, the suggested system makes use of deep learning architectures such as Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), ResNet, DenseNet, and VGG16. Achieving the maximum model accuracy while offering dependable and effective diagnostic support is the main goal of this study.The result shows that DenseNet provides a good accuracy of 96%.

articleTitle: A Blockchain Based Vehicular Ad-hoc System
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Advances in Computing and Communications (ICACC)
abstract: As connected vehicles become more prevalent, vehicular ad-hoc networks (VANETs) are being used to support vehicle-to-vehicle (V2V) and vehicle-to-infrastructure (V2I) communications for advanced driver-assistance systems (ADAS) and other intelligent services. However, secure communication is crucial in VANETs to prevent traffic accidents and ensure the safety of drivers and passengers. Many studies have been conducted on V2I authentication protocols, but most do not consider handover situations and can cause unnecessary computations, which can overload vehicles with limited computing resources. To address these issues, researchers have proposed a blockchain-based handover authentication protocol for VANETs. This protocol leverages the strength of blockchain technology to provide decentralization, data integrity, and transparency. It also ensures efficiency by only requiring lightweight computations during handover situations. The proposed protocol was subjected to formal analysis using Burrows–Abadi–Needham (BAN) logic, Real-Or-Random (ROR) oracle model, and Automated Validation of Internet Security Protocols and Applications (AVISPA) simulation. The researchers also conducted simulations using Network Simulator 3 (NS-3) to verify the practicality of the proposed protocol. Computational cost and security features of the proposed protocol were compared with existing protocols, demonstrating that the proposed protocol is more secure and efficient. Overall, the blockchain-based handover authentication protocol has the potential to improve the security and efficiency of VANETs, enabling safe and reliable communication between vehicles and infrastructure.

articleTitle: Crime Data Mapping Using HDFS for Data Visualization
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Advances in Computing and Communications (ICACC)
abstract: Crime data analysis is an important aspect of law enforcement and requires sophisticated techniques to uncover patterns and enhance predictive capabilities. This paper focuses on the mapping stage of crime data analysis, offering a thorough method for integrating Hadoop Distributed File System (HDFS) with the pre-clustering data using Haversine k-means algorithm for efficient crime data visualization. The ability to accurately identify and visually display spatial patterns and trends in criminal activity is of particular importance. Leveraging Haversine k-means clustering geo-location based grouping of crime data sets the foundation for subsequent mapping using HDFS. This integrated approach, which is an essential step towards improving decision making in the enforcement of legislation and urban planning, not only increases the effectiveness of crime data analysis but also facilitates accurate and efficient visualization.

articleTitle: Face Generation and Recognition in Forensic Science
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Advances in Computing and Communications (ICACC)
abstract: Suspect identification can be challenging for forensic investigations since standard procedures are time-consuming and prone to mistakes. This calls for the creation of novel approaches utilizing developments in machine learning (ML) and artificial intelligence (AI). In order to overcome these obstacles, the proposed Face Generation and Recognition in Forensic Science will make use of sophisticated recognition algorithms and AI-based face generation models. Fully trained Stable Diffusion model is applied to generate high-quality face images from textual descriptions. Image Generation, Text Guided Image Manipulation using Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models (DDPMs), and Dataset Matching are the three primary components of the process. Using a stable diffusion model, Image Generation quickly creates high-resolution images from word prompts by combining an autoencoder (VAE), U-Net, and text encoder. With the introduction of an alternate noise space for DDPMs, Text Guided picture Manipulation makes it possible to do meaningful picture altering tasks in response to text prompts. VGG-16 , a convolutional neural network architecture is used in dataset matching to extract features and calculate similarity, which makes dataset alignment and comparison easier. The suggested methodology gives law enforcement authorities effective tools for identifying suspects, which represents a substantial development in forensic investigations. The project intends to increase the efficiency of criminal investigations, accelerate the matching process with large datasets, and enhance the accuracy of facial sketches by utilizing AI and ML approaches. The approach’s ability to produce coherent and contextually relevant face images is validated by experimental results, which also show the approach’s potential for speeding up the conclusion of criminal cases, particularly unsolved cold cases. All things considered, Face Generation and Recognition in Forensic Science is a promising step in strengthening forensic science’s technological innovation capabilities.

articleTitle: GAN-Enhanced Brain Slice Images for Detecting Alzheimer’s Disease
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Advances in Computing and Communications (ICACC)
abstract: Alzheimer’s Disease (AD) is a progressive neurological disorder marked by cognitive decline, memory loss, and impaired reasoning, affecting millions globally. Early and accurate diagnosis of AD is crucial for managing the disease, yet traditional diagnostic methods such as clinical assessments and Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) face significant challenges. This research proposes a novel approach to enhance the diagnostic process by using Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) to improve brain MRI image quality, thereby aiding automated detection of AD. It involves preprocessing brain MRI scans, designing a GAN for image enhancement, and utilizing these enhanced images in a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) for detecting AD. The effectiveness of method is evaluated using key metrics such as accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity, comparing its performance to baseline methods using non-enhanced images. Cross-validation and testing with external datasets are conducted to ensure the model’s robustness and generalizability. The integrated GAN-CNN framework demonstrated a remarkable accuracy of 99.9 % in predicting AD using MRI images from the OASIS dataset.

articleTitle: Glaucoma Diagnosis From Smartphone Captured Fundus Images Using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Advances in Computing and Communications (ICACC)
abstract: The retina contains millions of photoreceptive cells called cones, rods, and blood vessels that nourish these cells. The optic nerve carries visual information from the retina to the brain. Glaucoma is a condition, where optic nerves get damaged often caused by high pressure within the eye. Fundus images provide rich information about the appearance of a patient’s retina and optic nerve head region. Even though there are various painless diagnosis methods, conventional fundus photography using Retcams is the most commonly used one. Examinations of the fundus images for structural abnormalities in the optic nerve head region such as increased cup-to-disc ratio, NRR thinning, and Violation of the ISNT rule provide sufficient evidence for the presence of glaucoma. However, conventional fundus imaging costs a lot concerning equipment and operation costs. Nowadays, smartphones can capture retina images and are a cheaper alternative to conventional fundus imaging using retcam devices. So our approach is to analyze smartphone-captured fundus images (SCFI) to detect the presence of glaucoma and provide accurate results at a lower cost. We designed an automated one-step approach-based glaucoma detection system that can detect the presence of glaucoma from smartphone-based fundus images with an accuracy of 93 percent. using a deep learning-based approach, The publicly available smartphone-captured fundus image dataset, BrG is used for conducting ablation studies.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Based Fault Diagnosis of Rolling Bearing Using Spectrogram and CWT Images of Vibration Data
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Advances in Computing and Communications (ICACC)
abstract: Rolling bearing plays an important role in fault detection of rotating machinery in the era of industrial 4.0. Very recently, machine learning based methods are gaining priority in automatic fault feature extraction and fault classification. Even though these are the promising field the presence of noise plays a vital role in fault diagnosis. To overcome this difficulty, this work is focused on a method based on Variational mode decomposition (VMD), Wavelet Threshold (WT) denoising and CNN based fault classification. Here VMD is used for decomposition, WT is used for denoising of each mode, and a well-known CNN named as AlexNet is used for Classification of Stacked STFT(S-STFT) and stacked CWT(S-CWT) images. Results show that S-CWT provides an accuracy value of 99.3% compared with S-STFT of accuracy 99.1%. Performance parameters like precision and recall also implicate the validation of the results.

articleTitle: IoT-Cloud Integration for Enhanced Container Weight Monitoring and Alerting: A Real-Time Solution
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Advances in Computing and Communications (ICACC)
abstract: Efficiently managing essential items in home utility containers is crucial for seamless daily operations. However, the inconvenience of not knowing when supplies are depleting can lead to unexpected shortages, causing disruptions and inconveniences. To address this, we present the "Smart Container Weight Monitoring System," an innovative solution that leverages Internet of Things (IoT) technology to enable real-time monitoring of container weights.

articleTitle: Impacts of Image Preprocessing Techniques on Lung Cancer Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Advances in Computing and Communications (ICACC)
abstract: The Computed Tomography (CT) scan is one of the most reliable imaging techniques radiologists employ to diagnose lung cancer. It provides a cross-sectional and more detailed visualization of the lung. Low Dose Computed Tomography (LDCT) is an effective way to reduce radiation risks associated with CT imaging. However, in practical use this will impose noise and other artifacts that account for the misdiagnosis of cancer. Image preprocessing is a necessary step before using CT scans for computer-aided lung cancer diagnosis to achieve accurate diagnostic results by reducing noise and other artifacts. Some of the key preprocessing methods for early lung cancer diagnosis are resampling, noise removal, Contrast Limited Adaptive Histogram Equalization (CLAHE), normalization, and augmentation. This work compares various image preprocessing scenarios for lung cancer classification using CT scan images. The quality of denoised images is assessed using metrics such as Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR), Mean Squared Error (MSE), Structural Similarity Index Measure (SSI), and Multi-scale Structural Similarity Index Measure (MSSI). Experimental results indicate that the wavelet filter outperforms other filters in terms of these metrics. ShuffleNet is a lightweight deep neural network used to evaluate the impact of various preprocessing scenarios on lung cancer classification. The results of this work demonstrate that preprocessing techniques like resampling, noise removal, CLAHE, normalization, and augmentation enhance the performance of ShuffleNet-based classification of lung cancer with an accuracy of 96.45%, precision of 100%, recall-93.83%, F1-score-96.82%, and AUC score of 99.55%.

articleTitle: Robust Direction of Arrival Estimation with Time Modulated Arrays using Modified MUSIC Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Advances in Computing and Communications (ICACC)
abstract: This paper proposes a robust direction of arrival estimation scheme using Modified MUSIC algorithm for Time-Modulated Linear Antenna arrays for, both coherent and non-coherent, low SNR signals. The performance of the proposed method is further verified for varying number of elements, inter-element spacing, incident angles, and SNR values and compared with the MUSIC algorithm. The simulation results show that direction of arrival estimation with Time Modulated Linear Array using Modified MUSIC performs better than MUSIC algorithm.

articleTitle: Detection of Road Attributes Using Solid-State LiDAR
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Advances in Computing and Communications (ICACC)
abstract: This paper introduces an enhanced approach for identifying and assessing road surface defects, particularly potholes, by utilizing LiDAR technology in conjunction with autonomous vehicles. By processing high-resolution LiDAR data, the system identifies significant deviations in road elevation, clusters potential potholes, and calculates their severity based on depth measurements. This automated approach offers precise, real-time monitoring of road conditions, significantly reducing the need for manual inspections. The integration of LiDAR technology with autonomous systems enhances road safety and maintenance efficiency, providing a scalable solution for proactive infrastructure management.

articleTitle: SwinLeafExplain: Interpretable Cotton Disease Classification with SWIN Transformer
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Advances in Computing and Communications (ICACC)
abstract: Healthy agriculture is vital for a nation’s prosperity. Cotton is a significant cash crop that is vulnerable to several leaf diseases that can lower yield, such as powdery mildew, army worm, bacterial blight, target spot, and aphids. To prevent further damage to crops, it is essential to discover these leaf diseases early. The early detection of cotton leaf disease is greatly aided by advancements in artificial intelligence. SwinLeafExplain, a novel approach for cotton leaf disease classification, leverages a SWIN Transformer model, known for its ability to capture intricate image patterns, potentially leading to more accurate disease detection. To enhance transparency for farmers and agricultural experts, SwinLeafExplain integrates explainability features using different class activation maps, allowing them to visualize the model’s reasoning behind classifications. SwinLeafExplain achieved exceptional performance with an accuracy of 99.72%. Our proposed method significantly outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in both accuracy and interpretability, providing valuable insights to aid agricultural decision-making.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Assisted Sanitizer Quality Identification Using Permittivity Measurement
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Advances in Computing and Communications (ICACC)
abstract: Sanitizers play a crucial role in hygiene and the prevention of infectious diseases by reducing harmful microorganisms on surfaces. This paper focuses on alcohol-based sanitizers, specifically those containing ethanol and isopropyl alcohol, known for their rapid action and broad spectrum efficacy. The effectiveness of these sanitizers depends on the alcohol content, with water enhancing their performance. Traditional quality detection methods are accurate but time-consuming. This work proposes a support vector machine based classification model combined with a complex permittivity measurement system to assess sanitizer quality. The model achieves 97.2% accuracy for a frequency range of 0.2–20 GHz at 25°C, with improved accuracy of 99% in the 2–5 GHz range, identifying this as the optimal frequency range for sanitizer classification. This method is compatible with any permittivity measurement system with measurement error ±15%. Significant time savings in quality assessment is also achieved.

articleTitle: Newton-Euler based Computational Modeling and Trajectory Planning in Human Arm Flexion-Extension Movements: A Preliminary Study for Collaborative Robot Implementation in Rehabilitation
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Advances in Computing and Communications (ICACC)
abstract: Human arm movement analysis is an important process in upper limb rehabilitation which helps in the restoration of motor function post injury. This will help in framing the strategies for rehabilitation with the aim of personalization and improved effectiveness. The current work focuses on modeling the human arm as a three-link system, representing the shoulder, elbow, and wrist joints. The arm’s mass, size, and flexion-extension limit angles are determined based on anthropometric data. These data are used for dynamic analysis, where a variable weight is placed at the fingertip and precisely simulated using the Newton-Euler approach. The torque variations along with the generated trajectory at each joint are significant, which can provide an analytical approach for understanding the arm dynamics that can lead to the implementation of collaborative robots in rehabilitation. This approach provides the tailor-made rehabilitation programs ensuring that robotic assistance is effectively aligned with the specific needs of the user.

articleTitle: Interpreting Temporal Dynamics in Distributed Fuzzy Cognitive Maps for Time Series Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Advances in Computing and Communications (ICACC)
abstract: Fuzzy Cognitive Maps (FCMs) are powerful tools for the modeling of complex systems, one of which is time series modeling. Although advocated for their interpretability, existing methods measure concept relevance based on static structural features often overlooking the dynamic influences over the time. This paper presents a novel SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) framework based Distributed FCM model. The proposed approach invokes functions to determine the SHAP concept relevance scores for the Distributed Fuzzy Cognitive Maps (DFCMs) for time series prediction, marginalizing over each concept and comparing the predicted states to an expected baseline iteratively. This method is interpreted as measuring the time-varying impact of each concept through the dynamic course of the system. The SHAP-based approach improves the interpretability and application of FCMs to the modeling of complex time-course systems.

articleTitle: T1W MRI to T2W MRI Image Synthesis Using SSIM-CycleGAN
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Advances in Computing and Communications (ICACC)
abstract: T1-weighted (T1W) and T2-weighted (T2W) sequences are common in MRI imaging, yet both are challenging to acquire efficiently. To optimize time and scanner availability, cross-modality image synthesis has emerged as a promising solution. The synthesis of T2-weighted MRI images from T1-weighted MRI images is essential in clinical practice, as it enables the extraction of valuable diagnostic information without requiring additional imaging sessions. Recently, CycleGAN networks have been widely utilized for synthesizing images from one modality to another due to their ability to be trained in an unsupervised manner. However, traditional CycleGANs often struggle to accurately capture structural and luminance information. Our proposed SSIM-CycleGAN integrates SSIM loss into the CycleGAN framework, resulting in a substantial improvement in the quality of the generated T2-weighted MRI images from T1-weighted MRI images. By focusing on structural similarity, this approach enhances both perceptual quality and clinical relevance. We conducted a detailed comparison of our method against existing techniques, and our proposed approach demonstrated significant improvements both quantitatively and qualitatively.

articleTitle: NearBySell : A Novel Approach to Localized E-Commerce with Focus on Seller-Customer Interaction and Enhanced Local Retail Network
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Advances in Computing and Communications (ICACC)
abstract: This paper examines a novel online retail application optimized for local commerce via a location-based matching system. The application supports the sale of new and secondhand items, home goods, and vegetables, requiring users to register and input their locations. Transactions occur only when the buyer’s and seller’s locations align, reducing logistical challenges. The system features a review mechanism allowing customers to rate sellers, influencing future buyer decisions and seller reputation. Security is ensured through hand-to-hand payments and direct seller delivery, mitigating risks associated with digital payments and third-party delivery. Additionally, the application supports long-term relationships by maintaining permanent connections between customers and sellers. Technical aspects include the development of location-based matching algorithms, review systems, and security measures. Notably, the application incorporates advanced security features such as fake reviews detection and duplicate listings detection to protect both buyers and sellers from fraudulent activities. This study highlights how these components enhance local market efficiency and e-commerce reliability.

articleTitle: A Comparative Analysis on Fashion Cloth Feature Extraction Methods using Text and Image Data
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Advances in Computing and Communications (ICACC)
abstract: Modern methods of extracting relevant features from images and texts are crucial to the recovery of fashionable garments. In this research, we compare and contrast a number of different approaches to extracting features from images and text. We utilize Generative Pre-trained Transformer (GPT) and Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) to efficiently process and represent textual descriptions of fashion products for text feature extraction. This allows us to take advantage of GPT's generative capabilities and contextual understanding. In order to extract features from photographs of fashion sketch images, we use a mix of Residual Networks (ResNet) and Visual Geometry Group (VGG) networks. This allows us to pick up complex visual patterns and details. Our method is designed to enhance the accuracy of text and image matching by combining the best features of these state-of-the-art models. Accuracy, recall, F1-score, and retrieval efficiency are some of the assessment metrics that were examined on a wide dataset that included different types of fashion clothing. The hybrid model improves feature extraction capabilities, producing robust and discriminative text and picture representations, according to preliminary findings. More intelligent and user-friendly retrieval systems in digital fashion platforms and e-commerce might be possible thanks to the study's useful insights into the possibilities of advanced deep learning architectures in the field of fashion product retrieval.

articleTitle: Design, Development, and Analysis of Spiral Microstrip Resonator Filter
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Advances in Computing and Communications (ICACC)
abstract: The study presents the design, simulation, and analysis of an electromagnetically coupled spiral resonator. The reflection and transmission characteristics of the spiral resonator coupled to a 50Ω microstrip line is studied in detail. The influence of geometric design and substrate parameters are analysed and design equations are derived. The presented design equations predicts the resonance frequency with an error less than 3%. A protype of the resonator is fabricated and the experimental analysis is carried out. The RFID tags and sensors can both be made with this spiral resonator sensor.

articleTitle: Advanced Machine Learning Approaches for Robust Credit Card Fraud Detection: A Comprehensive Evaluation and Practical Insights
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Advances in Computing and Communications (ICACC)
abstract: The critical issue of credit card fraud detection within the economic sector is addressed by developing robust predictive models to effectively identify financial fraud. Utilizing a diverse array of machine learning techniques, this study conducts a meticulous evaluation of each model’s strengths and limitations through key metrics such as accuracy, recall, precision, and F1-score. This comprehensive assessment provides insights into the comparative effectiveness of different algorithms and highlights the nuanced trade-offs in fraud detection methodologies. Beyond performance metrics, the research offers practical insights into the application of machine learning strategies in real-world scenarios, exploring best practices, identifying potential challenges, and suggesting avenues for improvement. By elucidating these aspects, the research aims to fortify fraud detection systems against evolving threats in the digital landscape, thereby enhancing the security and reliability of financial transactions.

articleTitle: Explainable AI Revolutionizing Kidney Transplants: Seeing Clearly to Save Lives
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Advances in Computing and Communications (ICACC)
abstract: Due to the inadequacies of sagacious matching systems, it has been established that there is a gross scarcity of donor kidneys; hence patients wait for a very long time. Because the medical data is so complicated and encompasses genetic compatibility, health history, and comorbidities, among others, finding the suitable match is difficult. In this paper, we propose an Explainable AI (XAI) model which predicts graft survival rates and complication risks using the SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) technique. The intention is to create a transparent model that enables doctors to merge data insights with their clinical experience. Through improvement of the donor-recipient matching processes, XAI thereby solves the problem of a deficit in organs and thus guarantees favorable outcomes for the patient since the Mean Squared Error is 0.089 for graft survival and 0.085 for complications. problem of organ deficit and promotes positive patient outcomes. Incorporating XAI into clinical decision-making processes does not only help speed up these decisions but also increase confidence among patients and physicians. The objective of this revolutionary approach is to alter kidney transplant surgery into a more effective, efficient and patient-centered practice as a way of combating the problem regarding organ scarcity.

articleTitle: Two Fingered Gripper Mechanism-based Mechatronics System for Borewell Rescue Operation
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Advances in Computing and Communications (ICACC)
abstract: This paper presents the development of a mechatronics system to carry out borewell rescue operation in a safe and efficient manner. Contrary to existing techniques dependent on manual pulley systems and ropes, this system is equipped with electric motors, a gripper, and a failsafe plate. These components enable it to navigate vertically and securely grip victims for rescue operations. The proposed system integrates a microcontroller-based control unit, a Wi-Fi supported camera module and electrical actuators for the motion control of the designed two fingered gripper mechanism. The proposed system improves the strength of two fingered gripper mechanism-based mechanical system by allowing the integration of vision assisted feedback and electrical actuation system.

articleTitle: Smart Blood Circulation Booster for Enhancing Cardiovascular Health in Hilly Regions Using IoT-Based Sensors and Thermoelectric Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Advances in Computing and Communications (ICACC)
abstract: The Smart Blood Circulation Booster (BCB) is designed to address suboptimal blood circulation in hilly regions by leveraging IoT-based sensors and thermoelectric technology. Integrating DS18B20 temperature sensors and pulse rate sensors, the system continuously monitors vital physiological parameters. The NodeMCU controller, utilizing advanced algorithms, dynamically adjusts a Thermoelectric Peltier module to regulate temperature and enhance blood circulation. This proactive solution not only monitors but actively improves the blood circulation, promoting cardiovascular health in challenging terrains. Preliminary results from trials involving participants aged 50-85 showed a significant increase in temperature by an average of 10%, indicating improved blood flow and validating the system's effectiveness.

articleTitle: Impact of Gate Oxide Thickness Variation on the On-state Safe Operating Area and FoM of SOI-Junctionless FinFET considering the Self-heating Effects
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Advances in Computing and Communications (ICACC)
abstract: A 3D Silicon On Insulator-Junctionless FinFET (SOI-JLFinFET) device structure has been simulated to explore the impact of gate oxide thickness (t<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ox</inf>) variation on performance metrics such as breakdown voltage, maximum drain current, and the safe operating area (SOA). To analyze the SOA thoroughly, simulations are done for SOI-JLFinFET with oxide thicknesses ranging from 2 nm to 5 nm. The effect of t<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ox</inf> on the peak temperature of SOI-JLFinFET is also studied. The distribution of the electric field vector in the channel region has been examined for both thin and thick gate oxides. The device’s performance for amplification application has also been assessed by obtaining the transconductance (g<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</inf>) at different drain voltages. Furthermore, the overall effect of gate oxide thickness (t<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ox</inf>) variation on the on-state breakdown voltage (V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">br,ON</inf>) and maximum drain current(I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">D,max</inf>), which impact the device’s power handling capability and Figure of Merit (FoM) have been studied.

articleTitle: Soil Monitoring and Crop Recommendation System via IoT and Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Advances in Computing and Communications (ICACC)
abstract: Traditional practices in agriculture lack the proper guidance in regard to crop production and yields, making the processes inefficient with Poor use of resources. To address the above challenges, we proposed an IoT and machine learning-based system targeting on the improvement of precision farming. The technology incorporated into our system is a microcontroller, numerous soil sensors and a GSM for transmitting the data. The main focus of our study is accurate crop recommendations that depend on which crops are suitable for the farmer and his environment. This is done via, evaluating some of the key factors of the environment in terms of Nitrogen, Phosphorous, and potassium Content in the soil, its Ph Level, the temperature, humidity and TDS. The way it works is that an image or a video of the soil is taken while, at the same time, it monitors the real-time data of the soil parameters using the sensors. Then it sends this data to a GSM module with IoT technology which connects to a model website on the cloud. The information is then processed by enhanced machine learning formulas in order to determine the fertility level of the soils and the type of crops to be grown on the land. The processed data and recommendations are sent back to the device with enabled user interface to see the analyzed results on a display. Here our use of IoT with machine learning enables the system give accurate and recommendable crop data, making the most of the resources and maximizing crop production. It bypasses the shortcomings of conventional ways of agricultural methods offering a scalable and efficient solution for modern agriculture.

articleTitle: Leveraging Acoustic Features and Deep Neural Architectures for Audio Deepfake Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Advances in Computing and Communications (ICACC)
abstract: This research presents a comparative analysis of various audio features and high-level architectures for deefake detection with emphasis on computational efficiency. Several light-weight models are proposed as opposed to GAN-based approaches in literature for evaluating custom-generated deep-fakes. The model is trained on Fake or Real dataset and achieved commendable performance using MFCC-Conformer and MFCC-LSTM feature-model combinations by achieving 87.61% and 87.52% accuracy, respectively. Specifically, the MFCC-Conformer recorded a TN of 526 and a FN of 18, along with an AUC score of 0.96, while the MFCC-DenseNet achieved a TN of 535, an FN of 9, and an AUC score of 0.96, underscoring their effectiveness in identifying fake audios. The outcomes underscore the effectiveness of the proposed models in combating the proliferation of misleading media content.
