articleTitle: Gaze Detection and Text Extraction from Images using CNN with DBSCAN-based Filter Design
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Advances in Computing and Communications (ICACC)
abstract: Gaze detection and text extraction are pivotal technologies in the domain of human-computer interaction and computer vision, enabling applications such as assistive technologies, user interface optimization, and automated content analysis. This paper presents a novel method that identifies the user’s gaze direction and extracts the necessary portion of text, which constitutes the user’s region of interest, using a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) integrated with a spatial attention mechanism. A Density-Based Spatial Clustering of Applications with Noise (DBSCAN)-based filter is incorporated into the system to remove textual noise from the extracted image, thereby improving the model’s accuracy and reducing computation time. The proposed method demonstrates reduced dependency on the CNN compared to previous approaches, resulting in enhanced real-time operation capability and lower latency. Computational optimization and real-time performance were thoroughly evaluated, showing that our system not only achieves high accuracy in gaze detection and text extraction but also maintains efficient processing speeds suitable for dynamic applications. This advancement offers significant improvements for applications in assistive technology, educational tools, and interactive media, where precise and efficient gaze detection and text extraction are critical.

articleTitle: Analysis and Implementation of Different Levels of Modified Hybrid Multilevel Inverter for Renewable Energy Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Advances in Computing and Communications (ICACC)
abstract: Multilevel inverters have become pivotal in modern power conversion systems, offering enhanced performance with higher output voltages and reduced harmonic distortions. This paper explores various multilevel inverter topologies focused on five-level, nine level etc and the various topologies. Simulation results using MATLAB Simulink demonstrate the effectiveness and practicality of this new inverter design. The efficacy of this scheme is confirmed through the demonstration of simulation results using MATLAB Simulink.

articleTitle: Melodic Precision: Unveiling the Impact of Recursive Feature Elimination on Music Genre Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Advances in Computing and Communications (ICACC)
abstract: Music genre classification has experienced significant advancements due to the integration of machine learning techniques. This study delves into the impact of the Recursive Feature Elimination (RFE) technique on the performance of music genre classification models. Utilizing the GTZAN dataset, which includes various audio features, we implement machine learning models such as Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, and Support Vector Machines (SVM). By employing the RFE technique, we aim to enhance model accuracy and interpretability. Analyzing classification metrics such as accuracy, precision, recall, F1 score, and confusion matrices, we provide a nuanced understanding of how feature selection and elimination using RFE refine the accuracy and interpretability of music genre classification models. Our findings reveal the effectiveness of RFE in improving the discriminative power of music genre classifiers, highlighting the importance of individual feature contributions. Additionally, our study compares the impact of RFE with other feature selection and elimination techniques such as variance threshold, Chisquare test, and information gain, offering valuable insights into optimizing music genre classification models for practical applications. These results underscore the potential of RFE to advance the field of music genre classification by improving model performance and interpretability, making it a valuable tool for researchers and practitioners in the domain.

articleTitle: Enhanced Solar Power Forecasting with CNNs Using Sky Imagery and Cloud Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Advances in Computing and Communications (ICACC)
abstract: The intermittent nature of solar power challenges the large scale integration of photovoltaics(PV) into electricity grids. Solar intermittency means fluctuation in power generation due to factors like irradiance, humidity, PV surface temperature etc. For the prediction of short-term fluctuations, deep learning using sky imagery is recognized as a promising approach for solar forecasting. Cloud changes in the sky are the primary driver of solar power fluctuations in short time intervals. This study proposes a CNN-based deep learning approach for short-term solar power forecasting using sky images. The model detects spatial and temporal trends that aid in precise prediction by utilizing a three-year collection of sky images and associated PV generation data. The model performs remarkably well on bright days, properly estimating solar power generation, as evidenced by evaluation criteria such as RMSE, MAE, and Forecast Skill (FS). Overall, it performs better than conventional persistence models, suggesting that there is a scope to improve the accuracy of solar power forecasts. The integration of cloud detection further enhances the model’s performance, allowing it to better differentiate between sunny and cloudy conditions.

articleTitle: NAIN: Real-Time Object Detection and Navigation Assistance for the Visually Impaired using Single Shot Detector Model
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Advances in Computing and Communications (ICACC)
abstract: Navigation for the Blind and Visually Impaired (BVI) poses a huge challenge due to lack of environmental cues. This research article proposes "NAIN" (Navigational Aid for the INsight-impaired) - an app for real-time object detection and navigation assistance for the BVI built using Python frameworks like Flask and OpenCV. Video frames from the camera are processed to recognize objects using the Single Shot Detector deep learning model implemented in TensorFlow. Detected objects are annotated with labels, proximity estimates, and communicated to the user via text-to-speech conversion and audio feedback. Object width in terms of pixels is mapped to real-world dimensions using the focal length of 500 pixels to provide distance estimates of objects like "Person detected at 300 cm". Quantitative testing shows over 90% accuracy in classifying daily objects. Distance approximation methodology provides 80% precise results for objects within 1000cm when properly calibrated. Initial trials illustrate reliable detection even in cluttered environments resulting in more confident indoor navigation. On the software architecture side, Flask enables graceful scaling of the detection pipeline across the client and server. HTML and CSS used in crafting an accessible interface optimized for use via screen readers. The system is designed for computational efficiency working in real-time without internet connectivity. It provides a template to develop affordable assisted perception for the BVI using computer vision. Future efforts look to enrich object libraries, integrate mapping APIs for outdoor settings, and provide navigation vectors around obstacles. By converting visual data into meaningful and intuitive audio cues, to raise awareness that can empower the BVI with greater mobility and independence.

articleTitle: Improving PM 2.5 Prediction Accuracy with a Hybrid EEMD-CNN-BiLSTM Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Advances in Computing and Communications (ICACC)
abstract: Due to its detrimental impact on both the environment and human health, air pollution is a major global health concern. One of the main causes of Delhi’s air pollution is particulate matter (PM 2.5), and exposure to it, whether short-term or long-term, can have detrimental effects on one’s health. Effective prediction of PM 2.5 is crucial for improving accuracy and reducing the impact of severe pollution events, which enhances decision-making related to environmental management. However, accurate forecasting of PM 2.5 levels is challenging due to the unpredictable nature of the data. In this proposed strategy, EEMD based decomposition algorithm is employed to de-noise the PM 2.5 data. EEMD decomposes the pollution data into 9 IMFs and one residue component. Then, the CNN-BiLSTM predictive model is apply to each extracted IMF as well as the residue component. Afterwards, the predicted results of each component obtained using CNN-BiLSTM are added to determine the final forecast. To validate the effectiveness of the hybrid method, its performance is compared against other models, such as traditional BiLSTM and conventional CNN-BiLSTM, using statistical error metrics including MAE, RMSE and R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The proposed model yields an MAE of 7.77, an RMSE of 11.86, and an R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> value of 0.99. The empirical results demonstrate that the proposed hybrid approach, based on EEMD-CNN-BiDLSTM, outperforms traditional methods in terms of prediction accuracy.

articleTitle: ICACC 2024 Author Index
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Advances in Computing and Communications (ICACC)

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of SLAM-based Autonomous Navigation of Mobile Robot
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Advances in Computing and Communications (ICACC)
abstract: This work, investigated an autonomous mobile robot simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM) using the Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) in an indoor environment. All of the experiments were run using the Robot Operating System (ROS). In the actual trials, the 2D laser scan matching data was acquired using the Rplidar A1 single-line lidar, and the indoor map was created using the open-source Gmapping and Hector SLAM algorithms, which may obtain the indoor maps in the ROS graphical tool Rviz. An autonomous mobile robot for simultaneous localization and mapping is possible and high-precision maps may be created, according to the experimental results of the two open-source algorithms with and without sensor fusion analyzed.

articleTitle: Forecast PV Generation, EV Charging Schedule and Energy Load Demand for Optimal Power Scheduling in P2P Nanogrid Network
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Advances in Computing and Communications (ICACC)
abstract: This paper presents optimal power scheduling for peer-to-peer (P2P) nanogrid networks incorporating photovoltaic (PV) and electric vehicle (EV) resources. The aim is to minimize energy cost, maximize self-consumption of PV power, and reduce grid dependency through coordinated scheduling of EV charging and P2P energy trading. In this approach, EVs are considered not only as loads but also as energy-sharing partners, contributing to the dynamic energy landscape of the network. The primary objective is to develop an optimal solution for the power scheduling in the nanogrid network. After forecasting, the dataset are given to an optimization module using particle swarm optimization (PSO) to minimize the energy costHere, PV generation data, EV charging schedules, and energy load demand are forecasted using Bidirectional - Long Short Term Memory (BD-LSTM) models. An objective function was formulated for optimal power scheduling, and optimized using PSO.

articleTitle: The Impact of Optimization Techniques on Cancer Classification with Gene Expression Data
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Advances in Computing and Communications (ICACC)
abstract: Cancer classification using gene expression profiling is a fundamental component of cancer research and development, because it contributes to the identification of cancer subtypes as well as the identification of proper treatments for patients. The purpose of this paper is to assess the efficiency in classification of different optimization algorithms. PCA, GA, FI, SFS, and VT methods are applied for the feature selection on gene expression data. The selected features are then passed into a Gaussian Naive Bayes classifier to classify it into a particular class. In order to compare the efficiency of each presented optimization technique we calculate various evaluation metrices, and CPU time. To overcome the shortcomings of both the high accuracy methods, we proposed a new approach that integrates VT and GA. The outcomes of this work help to contribute to the research of the best combination of optimization tools for accurate classification of cancer, which will help further develop the concept of precision medicine and individualized therapy.

articleTitle: Effect of Pneumatic Based Hybrid Robotic Gripper for Safer Handling of Complex Geometries
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Advances in Computing and Communications (ICACC)
abstract: The present research work mainly concentrates on development of hybrid grippers with the integration of hard and soft components for achieving object manipulation. By combining pneumatic actuation with mechanical fingers, complex geometries can be handled effectively. Pneumatic hybrid gripper fabricated with PLA and silicone rubber offers adaptability and versatility. Resistive sensors over silicone surface of gripper lead to cost-effective force detection and tactile sensing. The proposed gripper was designed and analyzed using Fusion 360 and ANSYS. Inflatable silicone rubber and gripper body were fabricated using liquid casting and Fused Deposited Modelling 3D printing techniques. Real-time feedback sensors were employed with fabricated gripper to get better performance. Testing proves its capability to handle loads up to 500g with a force of 3.3N. Finally, the assembled hybrid gripper offers a versatile solution for robotic manipulation, ensuring stability and minimizing damage across various industries.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of CNN Model for Digit Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Advances in Computing and Communications (ICACC)
abstract: Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) are the key constructors of deep neural networks, which mimics the human brain activity. CNN models rely on convolution operation performed on images with different filters or kernels, that helps to identify certain key aspects of an image. However, in order to activate such a convolution process, activation functions are required and optimizers are then used to further optimize the operation. There are several activation functions and optimizers available, based on which the scale of efficiency of the model varies. In this paper, analysis of different combinations of optimizers and activation functions for the CNN model has been done and resulted in a most suitable and efficient combination, which produced a promising result of 99.2% accuracy on a general architecture.

articleTitle: An Intelligent IoT Solution with Real-Time Monitoring for Road Safety
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Advances in Computing and Communications (ICACC)
abstract: Driver drowsiness is the major reason for accidents, as per the research conducted all over India in October 2023. Paper introduces an innovative IoT solution aimed at combating accidents resulting from drowsy driving. Leveraging Raspberry Pi, alcohol sensor, GPS, ultrasonic sensor, ADC, WiFi, and IoT connectivity enables real-time monitoring. Central to its functionality is the integration of Convolution Neural Network (CNN) algorithms for accurate drowsiness detection. The Raspberry Pi serves as the central processing unit, coordinating data collection and analysis from multiple sensors. The alcohol sensor detects alcohol levels, while the ultrasonic sensor identifies obstacles on the road. GPS technology tracks the vehicle’s location, aiding navigation and emergency response. ADC ensures precise sensor measurements. WiFi and IoT connectivity enable seamless data transfer to remote servers for analysis. IoT provides timely alerts to prevent accidents caused by drowsy driving. Behavioral features are non intrusive and is used for monitoring the driver. Analysis of data dumped in the server aims to refine algorithms, improve accuracy, and enhance effectiveness in preventing accidents by using the dataset for training of deep learning algorithm, ensuring continuous optimization of the system. For accident prevention, once the drowsiness is detected in the server, speed control of the vehicle and informing relatives via IoT can be considered as future work.

articleTitle: Ensemble-Based Deep Learning Approach for Characterization of Thyroid Nodules in Ultrasound Imaging
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Advances in Computing and Communications (ICACC)
abstract: This paper addresses the challenge of distinguishing between benign and malignant thyroid nodules using ultrasound (US) imaging, which can be particularly difficult for less experienced clinicians. To aid in this diagnostic process, the paper proposes an ensemble-based classification model that leverages pretrained convolutional neural network (CNN) models. The model combines the outputs of fine-tuned pretrained networks using various ensemble learning strategies, including two-level stacking, three-level stacking, and weighted average ensemble (WAE). The proposed model is evaluated using the DDTI dataset, demonstrating that the ensemble approach offers more promising results and superior prediction accuracy compared to individual models. These findings highlight the potential of these models to assist healthcare professionals in diagnosing thyroid nodules more accurately, thereby enabling timely and appropriate treatment and increasing patient survival rates.

articleTitle: Digital Watermarking in Astrocytoma Brain Tumor MRI Images Using Discrete Stockwell Transform
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Advances in Computing and Communications (ICACC)
abstract: An efficient digital watermarking system for embedding Electronic Patient’s Record in brain tumor MRI images using Discrete Orthonormal Stockwell Transform for telemedicine applications is presented in this article. The patient details such as name, sex and age are embedded as a watermark in astrocytoma brain tumor MRI images. Initially local binary pattern features of the MRI image are extracted. These LBP features are used to find out the scaling and embedding factors which are the keys used for embedding as well as extraction. System performance is analysed using different performance measures like Peak Signal to Noise Ratio (PSNR), Structural Similarity Index (SSIM) and Normalized Cross Correlation (NCC). A large value of PSNR value of 96.29 dB is obtained with an embedding coefficient of 38.5 which indicates that the watermarking has not affected the quality of MRI image. The NCC between the embedded and extracted watermark is 1 which indicates that the extraction process has perfectly recovered the watermark without any alteration or distortion and the system has the ability to withstand attacks.

articleTitle: Path Tracing and Validation of Omni Wheeled Mini Robot Using Visual Feedback
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Advances in Computing and Communications (ICACC)
abstract: Holonomic drives are gaining popularity in many fields due to their versatility in various industrial applications. The ability of the holonomic drive robots to move in all directions makes it distinct from other drive mechanisms. Open-loop control of omnidirectional bots can be achieved with relative ease whereas automating it is not as easy. When trying to create an automated system with lower cost, off the shelf components and hardware, other problems may arise as a result of the poor performance of the components. Here a three wheeled omnidirectional robot that can trace a predefined path without human intervention has successfully been developed.

articleTitle: Design of a PTAT and Bandgap Current Reference with On-chip Digital Calibration
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Advances in Computing and Communications (ICACC)
abstract: This paper presents the implementation of a bandgap current and proportional to absolute temperature (PTAT) current reference circuits. An on-chip digital calibration circuit is incorporated into the circuits to compensate for the effect of process-induced variations. A start-up circuit that functions without any external signal is also included in the bandgap. The circuits were designed and fabricated in 180 nm CMOS process. The circuits operate with a supply voltage of 1.8V and occupy a total area of 312 × 210 µm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The combined power consumption of the bandgap and PTAT circuits is 210 µW. Measurements in the fabricated test chip show that the bandgap circuit generates a current of 19.2 µA at ambient temperature and exhibits a temperature coefficient of 110 ppm/°C over a temperature range of 0 to 100 °C. The PTAT circuit was observed to generate a current of 3.6 µA at ambient temperature with a slope of 0.014 µA/°C over a temperature range of 0 to 100 °C.

articleTitle: Verifiability and Visibility of the Data Modification in cloud using Enhanced Attribute Based Encryption(ABE)
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Advances in Computing and Communications (ICACC)
abstract: Applications, data, and infrastructure hosted on cloud servers benefit from a range of cybersecurity measures aimed at safeguarding them. Utilizing techniques like identity and access management, data loss prevention, and various technologies, combined with security policies and controls, serves to protect cloud environments from internal threats, unauthorized access, and online attacks. Maintaining data privacy in cloud platforms necessitates encryption, ensuring that only authorized entities can access and decrypt the data. In this study, we propose an attribute-based encryption (ABE) method, specifically employing ciphertext policies (CP-ABE), to restrict file data viewing and editing solely to authorized users. We introduce additional features such as email notifications and file update status tracking. This research investigates the effectiveness of ABE in ensuring secure data modification, offering insights into its potential for maintaining integrity and transparency in cloud-based data storage.

articleTitle: Seismic Spectrogram based Elephant Detection System
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Advances in Computing and Communications (ICACC)
abstract: This paper presents the design, development, and implementation of a real-time seismic-based elephant detection system aimed at mitigating human-elephant conflicts. The system leverages geophones to detect seismic infrasound signals produced by elephant movements. A low-noise amplifier conditions the weak seismic signals, which are then digitized and processed using an Arduino-based microcontroller. Advanced signal processing techniques, including spectral analysis and feature extraction, are employed to distinguish elephant rumbles from background noise such as environmental vibrations. The system provides early-warning capabilities through audible alarms and SMS alerts, offering immediate notification to authorities and local communities. The proposed detection mechanism demonstrates high sensitivity and specificity, making it an effective solution for both real-time monitoring and data collection for long-term conservation efforts. The system’s low-cost, energy-efficient design makes it suitable for deployment in remote wildlife habitats, contributing to sustainable conservation practices and enhancing human safety in areas prone to wildlife intrusions.

articleTitle: Identification of Fake Medicinal Raw Materials using Machine Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Advances in Computing and Communications (ICACC)
abstract: This paper extends the methodology for leaf classification by utilizing ResNet50, particle swarm optimization for hyperparameter tuning (PSO), and support vector machines (SVM) to classify 30 species, compared to the previous work that classified 7 species. The proposed approach pulls down the powerful feature extraction capabilities of ResNet50, optimized through PSO for hyperparameter tuning, and classified with SVM. By incorporating these advanced techniques, our approach achieves a high accuracy of 99.51%, which significantly outperforms previous methods. The scalability and robustness of this combined model are thoroughly demonstrated through extensive experimentation and evaluation on a comprehensive dataset of over 3500 leaf images. The results highlight significant improvements in classification performance, showing the model’s effectiveness in handling a larger and more diverse set of species. This advancement underscores the potential for broader applications in various fields, including botanical studies, agricultural automation, and environmental monitoring. By providing a scalable solution that maintains high accuracy, our methodology can be utilized for large-scale plant identification and monitoring systems, contributing to more efficient agricultural practices and better understanding of plant biodiversity. The promising results set a new benchmark for research and development in the domain of leaf classification in future, encouraging further exploration of deep learning techniques and optimization methods to enrich classification accuracy and applicability across different plant species and environmental conditions.

articleTitle: Leveraging Hybrid Machine Learning Technique For Effective House Rental Price Forecasting
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Advances in Computing and Communications (ICACC)
abstract: These days, figuring out the house's sale price is crucial because both the land and the house's prices rise annually. Therefore, the next generation needs a simple approach for forecasting future rents for houses. Accurate and data-driven strategies are crucial for estimating house rental prices in the rapidly shifting real estate market. This study investigates the application of machine learning to accurate rental price forecasting. Conventional methods of rental estimation tend to rely on intuition and knowledge of the marketplace in the area, but they are incapable of taking into consideration the complex network of variables which influence rental rates. This study explores how rental prices are influenced by factors including the age of the property, whether it is furnished, the flat area, the size of the house etc. It also shows how machine learning models may be used to find hidden connections and get precise rental price predictions. The dearth of highly accurate models currently in use, the need to reduce overpricing, adjust to changing conditions in the market, maximize the return on investments, support data-driven decision-making, advance market transparency, and create a simple to use interface are among the reasons behind this research. The main goal is to create a reliable and accurate model for predicting the price of a rental home so that tenants and property owners can benefit from data-driven insights.

articleTitle: Hate Speech Detection in Social Media Using BiLSTM
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Advances in Computing and Communications (ICACC)
abstract: Social media platforms also function as breeding grounds for hate speech. Hate speech is offensive language targeting people based on their characteristics, including gender, race, or religion. The existing hate speech detection system relies on sentiment analysis, which is limited to processing static data that has been extracted from social media platforms beforehand. This research focuses on the development of a hate speech detection system specifically designed for social media platforms. By utilizing Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM) networks, the proposed system seeks to precisely detect and categorize hate speech in real time, allowing for rapid mitigation and intervention measures. The network can grasp both past and future context by processing text inputs bidirectionally, enabling a thorough comprehension of semantic linkages and linguistic nuances. The system integrates a chat evaluator module to monitor real-time conversations, issuing warnings and blocking users based on a threshold of detected hate speech occurrences. The implementation of a bidirectional strategy improves the model's overall accuracy and decreases false positives by enhancing its capacity to identify minute fluctuations in hate speech patterns. This initiative contributes to the continuous endeavors aimed at combating hate speech, thereby fostering a digital environment that is more inclusive and secure.

articleTitle: Malayalam Fake News Detection Using Optimized Convolutional Neural Network (OPCNN)
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Advances in Computing and Communications (ICACC)
abstract: These days, a range of issues are being caused by fake news, including satirical pieces, fake news, and intentional government propaganda. Because of the blathering social media discourse, the idea of "fake news" has recently evolved. Wide-ranging consequences of fake news dissemination include the development of distorted opinions and the tampering of election outcomes to benefit specific politicians. Spammers also use captivating news headlines to entice readers to click on their advertisements. These days, it can be quite difficult to tell if the news we hear is accurate. There aren’t many methods for assessing authenticity, and the ones that are accessible are all difficult and beyond the capabilities of the average person. A fact-checking platform that gives us that chance is desperately needed. Deep Learning (DL) approaches are suited for more accurately and efficiently detecting false news because of their recent accomplishments in difficult natural language processing tasks. The suggested approach is a multi-layered, optimal CNN model for detecting fake news. The OPCNN and Word embedding are optimized for feature extraction using the hyperopt optimization method in order to produce highly accurate results. In this study, we generated word embeddings using the FastText technique. The purpose of the model is to identify news stories published in Malayalam that are either false or misleading. The model is trained on 80% of a newly compiled Malayalam dataset consisting of news articles from various online sources having 11,686 news items with 5843 false and real news entries apiece and then evaluated on the remaining 20%. The evaluation’s findings show that the suggested model works better than current methods and has a high degree of accuracy when it comes to identifying false information in Malayalam.

articleTitle: Responsible AI Framework For Large Language Models (LLMs)
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Advances in Computing and Communications (ICACC)
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have become quite popular in recent years due to their remarkable capacity to produce language that is human-like. The creation and use of LLMs, however, also bring up serious ethical questions on topics like prejudice, discrimination, privacy, security, transparency, and unexpected consequences. Responsible AI frameworks for LLMs are becoming more and more necessary in order to solve these issues. A responsible AI framework can offer direction on how to create and use LLMs in a way that is morally right, just, and advantageous for everyone. This paper covers important factors for creating responsible AI frameworks for LLMs and emphasizes the need for such frameworks. Transparency, justice, privacy, responsibility, safety, and social duty are some of these factors. We can ensure that these models are created and used in a way that is consistent with societal values and goals and that they help to create a better and more just world by adopting a responsible AI framework for LLMs.

articleTitle: Detection of Sleep Apnea: A Comparative Analysis of Advanced Machine Learning and Deep Learning Approaches
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Advances in Computing and Communications (ICACC)
abstract: Sleep apnea is a prevalent and serious sleep disorder caused by breathing interruptions during sleep, which is lead to critical health issues like cardiovascular diseases. Traditional diagnostic methods, such as polysomnography, are often very large process, costly, and not easily accessible, highlighting the need for automated and affordable detection solutions. This review paper examines the utilization of machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) methods for detecting and diagnosing sleep apnea. We offer a thorough overview of the current research, analyzing various studies that utilize different data types, including electrocardiogram (ECG), electroencephalogram (EEG), and photoplethysmography (PPG) signals. The review assesses the effectiveness of different algorithms, feature extraction techniques, and the integration of multiple signal types to improve detection accuracy. By summarizing key developments and identifying existing challenges, we aim to outline future research directions to enhance the robustness, interpretability, and real-time identification of sleep apnea using machine learning and deep learning techniques.

articleTitle: Exploring Explainable AI in Large Language Models: Enhancing Transparency and Trust
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Advances in Computing and Communications (ICACC)
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are at the forefront of technological evolution, significantly enhancing digital interactions and automating complex processes across various sectors. While these models facilitate advancements in data analytics, content generation, and strategic decision-making, their opaque nature poses challenges regarding user trust and model comprehension. Addressing the critical need for transparency, this paper focuses on enhancing LLM explainability. We propose a framework to demystify the internal mechanisms of these models, facilitating a deeper understanding that aligns with stringent ethical standards. Our approach integrates advanced explanatory tools that elucidate model decisions and foster accountability and fairness in Artificial Intelligence applications. Through rigorous analysis and the development of novel interpretative methodologies, we aim to bridge the gap between LLM capabilities and ethical AI practices, ensuring that these powerful tools are leveraged responsibly and transparently in critical infrastructures.

articleTitle: Personalized Music Recommendation: A Comparative Study of Machine Learning and Deep Learning Approaches
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Advances in Computing and Communications (ICACC)
abstract: The rapid advancement of music playback technology, particularly within mobile platforms, has fundamentally transformed user engagement with music. Despite significant improvements in music retrieval techniques over the past decade, the evolution of music recommendation systems remains in its early stages. With users having access to extensive online music libraries, the task of selecting preferred tracks from an overwhelming array of options presents a considerable challenge. Individual musical tastes vary widely, and the influx of new users and music necessitates a system that can adapt dynamically.Personalized music recommendation systems face the dual challenge of managing vast amounts of data while delivering accurate results, making them resource-intensive. However, the high precision of these models drives their increasing application in commercial settings. This paper proposes a framework aimed at enhancing recommendation accuracy by tailoring suggestions to align more closely with user preferences.A comprehensive analysis of traditional and advanced music recommendation methodologies is presented, focusing on two user-centric approaches: user preference and emotion-based metrics. These methodologies are critically compared, leveraging the Million Song Dataset (MSD) for training the recommendation system. Additionally, an Android application has been developed to collect empirical data on user experiences, facilitating a deeper understanding of user interactions and satisfaction with the recommendation framework. This research aims to improve user experience in music discovery by providing more relevant and personalized recommendations.

articleTitle: Analyzable Metaphase Image Selection Using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Advances in Computing and Communications (ICACC)
abstract: Identification of good metaphase is a prerequisite and an essential step in human karyotyping which is used for analysis of genetic abnormalities in human beings. Most of the research work is focused on automation of karyotyping process but despite being crucial step, very scant attention is given to metaphase image selection. The conventional method, still used by cytogeneticists is a manual visual search of good metaphase spread from microscopic slides. This system is highly dependent on individual observations and suffers from drawbacks such as complexity, tediousness, subjective, time consuming and needs a trained expertise. In this study, we propose a novel approach for the selection of analyzable metaphase images using three publicly available datasets. We evaluated seven critical features namely chromosome spread quality, morphology, focus and clarity, staining quality, metaphase stage, background, and field of view for classification of metaphase images using deep learning models, including MobileNetV2, ResNet50, DenseNet121, VGG16, and EfficientNetBO. Among these, EfficientNetBO outperformed the others, establishing a new baseline for this application. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work to employ publicly available datasets for the automated selection of analyzable metaphase images. Moreover, our proposed method can run efficiently on any platform with a Python interpreter installed, achieving high classification performance and flexibility.

articleTitle: Utilizing Neural Networks To Analyze Respiratory Sounds For The Detection Of Lung Diseases
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Advances in Computing and Communications (ICACC)
abstract: Respiratory disorders, such as bronchitis and asthma, present significant global health challenges that require timely and accurate diagnosis for effective treatment. Traditional methods of diagnosing these conditions rely on manual analysis of lung sound recordings, which is time-consuming and prone to errors. This project introduces a novel automated diagnostic system leveraging advanced machine learning techniques to enhance diagnostic accuracy and efficiency. By employing deep learning methods, specifically Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCCs), Continuous Short-Time Fourier Transform (CSTFT), and mel spectrograms for feature extraction, we developed a proprietary convolutional neural network (CNN) architecture. This architecture processes each audio feature type separately before integrating them into a cohesive model. Our extensive testing demonstrates that the system achieves a remarkable classification accuracy of 90.49% for respiratory illnesses. This innovative approach not only streamlines the diagnostic process but also provides a reliable tool for medical professionals, facilitating early detection and improved treatment planning for respiratory disorders.

articleTitle: Feature Importance and Model Performance in Deep Learning for Speech Emotion Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Advances in Computing and Communications (ICACC)
abstract: Speech emotion recognition (SER) is detecting a person’s emotional state through their voice, a technique now widely applied across various fields. This paper aims to explore the significance of different acoustic features in SER using the TESS dataset, which comprises approximately 2800 audio files featuring 200 words spoken by two female actors, representing seven emotions: anger, disgust, fear, happiness, pleasant surprise, sadness, and neutrality. We extracted seven key acoustic features from these audio files: Chromas, Mel Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCCs), Mel spectrogram, Zero crossing rate, RMS power, contrast, and pitch. Our study involved applying LSTM and CNN deep learning methods to assess the performance of each feature. Results indicate that the MFCC feature performs better, with accuracy exceeding 99% in LSTM and CNN models. Additionally, we employed traditional machine learning models, specifically random forest and decision tree classifiers, combined with a grid search feature selection method to generate feature importance graphs. These results highlight pitch as the most critical feature in both models. However, pitch alone yielded only 28% accuracy in LSTM and CNN models. This discrepancy underscores the complex interplay between feature selection and model architecture in optimizing SER performance. Our findings reveal critical insights into the interplay between feature relevance and model efficacy, highlighting the necessity of feature optimization for enhancing SER systems.

articleTitle: AI-Driven Diagnostics: Comparative Analysis of Machine Learning and Deep Learning Approaches in Multiple Sclerosis Diagnostics
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Advances in Computing and Communications (ICACC)
abstract: Multiple Sclerosis (MS) is a chronic autoimmune disorder that targets the central nervous system, resulting in considerable physical and cognitive disabilities. Timely and precise diagnosis is essential for the effective management and treatment of Multiple Sclerosis (MS). Predicting MS involves using various types of data to assess the risk and diagnose the disease. The data commonly used are clinical, imaging, speech and gene data. This work presents a review of machine learning and deep learning methods, encompassing a broad spectrum of algorithms such as Support Vector Machines (SVM), Random Forest (RF), eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), and Artificial Neural Networks (ANNs). Furthermore, the survey gives a comparative analysis of the dataset used, algorithms employed and the performance metrics. The survey also compares the implemented results with DL using the gene data. It also identifies current challenges in MS prediction, such as heterogeneity of MS, integration of multimodal data, validation and clinical implementation. Our goal is to offer a valuable resource for researchers and practitioners.

articleTitle: Improving Obfuscated Malware Classification: A Machine Learning Approach with Feature Selection and Data Balancing
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Advances in Computing and Communications (ICACC)
abstract: Obfuscated malware refers to malicious software that has been deliberately modified to hide its malicious purpose and avoid detection by conventional security mechanisms. Classifying obfuscated malware poses a significant challenge due to its deceptive nature and the dynamic techniques used by attackers to obfuscate code. Existing approaches in malware analysis often struggle to accurately classify obfuscated malware, leading to potential security vulnerabilities and data breaches. In this research, we investigate the application of machine learning algorithms for malware analysis, specifically focusing on multi-class classification of obfuscated malware using the CIC-MalMem-2022, a latest dataset. We apply data preprocessing techniques, including Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) and normalization, to enhance the dataset's balance and consistency. Subsequently, we train and evaluate various machine learning algorithms, including Random Forest (RF), XGBoost, K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), LightGBM, and Decision Trees (DT), on different datasets comprising SMOTE, normalized, and SMOTE+normalized instances. Our study also explores the effect of feature selection process on the performance of the model. We identify the top 35 features for optimal accuracy, addressing the dimensionality challenge inherent in large-scale datasets. Our findings reveal that the Random Forest (RF) model achieves the highest accuracy of 96.23% on the dataset that is balanced by SMOTE with top 35 features.

articleTitle: GeoChromNet: Declustering Metaphase Chromosomes via Topology-Informed Deep Instance Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Advances in Computing and Communications (ICACC)
abstract: Accurate segmentation and declustering of metaphase chromosomes are crucial for automated karyotyping and diagnosing genetic disorders. However, the complex arrangements in metaphase spreads, including overlapping and touching chromosomes, challenge existing segmentation approaches. This paper presents GeoChromNet (Geometric Chromosome Network), a novel deep learning architecture utilizing topological information to enhance metaphase chromosome instance segmentation and declustering. Our model combines a modified Mask R-CNN backbone with a topology-aware module to effectively segment and decluster chromosomes. We evaluate GeoChromNet on two datasets along with augmentation: The Cell Image Library (CIL), with 5,000 metaphase cell images and 229,852 annotations across 24 chromosome classes, and the BioImage Chromosome Classification Dataset (BICCD), containing 42 chromosome objects with various annotations. Experimental results show GeoChromNet outperforms state-of-the-art methods like ChroSegNet, Mask R-CNN, PSPNet, and DeepLabV3. On the CIL dataset, GeoChromNet achieves a Mean Pixel Accuracy (MPA) of 96.8%, an F1 score of 0.945, a Mean Intersection over Union (MIoU) of 0.921, a Jaccard index of 0.893, and a Dice similarity coefficient of 0.937. These results represent improvements of 2.3%, 3.1%, 3.7%, 4.2%, and 2.8% respectively over the next best model, ChroSegNet. GeoChromNet’s topology-informed approach is particularly effective in declustering challenging cases of overlapping and touching chromosomes, as evidenced by a 15.% increase in cluster separation accuracy compared to ChroSegNet. On the BICCD dataset, GeoChromNet maintains its superior performance, achieving an MPA of 95.7% and an F1 score of 0.932, demonstrating its robustness across different datasets. Our work highlights the potential of integrating topological information into deep learning models to improve the accuracy and robustness of metaphase chromosome segmentation and declustering, paving the way for more reliable automated karyotyping systems.

articleTitle: ECG Signal Classification and Anomaly Detection using LSTM and HMM Models
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Advances in Computing and Communications (ICACC)
abstract: Accurate detection and classification of electrocardiogram (ECG) signals is required for cardiac condition diagnosis and timely medical intervention. However, capturing the complex temporal dependencies in ECG data is difficult and hence may provide less effective performance comparatively. The project proposes an innovative approach to detecting and classifying the anomalies in ECG using LSTM and HMM. Preprocessing and normalization of the ECG data are done. After that, the sequence is prepared for input in LSTM, which builds a strong LSTM model with reinforced regularization techniques designed for feature learning from the ECG data. The features extracted by LSTM were concatenated with the original features and applied to train the HMM for anomaly detection based on estimating the likelihood of the log probabilities. Thresholding the log probabilities will locate anomalies. The next step is the implementation of HMM to classify ECG signals. The proposed method shows the framework comprehensively for effective detection of anomaly and classification, combining the strong points of both LSTM and HMM. The results obtained are employed to illustrate and prove the efficiency of the proposed combined approach and emphasise the importance of the combination of deep learning and statistical models for further analysis of ECG signals.

articleTitle: AI Meets Cyber Defense: Enhancing Network Security with GAN-Driven NIDS
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Advances in Computing and Communications (ICACC)
abstract: The field of cybersecurity has witnessed a growth in the breadth and intricacy of cyber threats due to the advancement of communication technology, which calls for the implementation of strong network intrusion detection systems (NIDS). Regrettably, a wide range of potential hazards might put computer users at risk when using the Internet. Users stand to lose a great deal, including control over machines, private information, and potentially even identity theft. The ongoing problem of inconsistent and changing threat data persists despite notable improvements in NIDS models. As more and more research has realized the need for improved detection skills, artificial intelligence (AI) has become a viable answer. In order to meet the challenges presented by emerging cyber threats, this study presents a thorough investigation into the integration of AI, specifically generative adversarial networks (GANs), into NIDS. GANs are a machine learning breakthrough that provides a fresh method for creating new data instances that closely mimic real data. This skill is especially useful in the context of network intrusion detection systems (NIDS), where identifying anomalies necessitates a sophisticated comprehension of intricate and dynamic threat patterns. Our study expands on earlier research in the field that mostly concentrated on deep learning methods like autoencoders, convolutional neural networks (CNN), and long short-term neural networks (LSTM), as well as conventional machine learning models like decision trees (DT) and support vector machines (SVM). Although these methods have shown potential, there hasn’t been much of a practical use for them in actual NIDS systems. A promising approach to improving NIDS performance is provided by the suggested NIDS makes use of GANs, especially when it comes to anomaly detection. Through the creation of artificial data instances that closely resemble real-world threats, GANs can enhance the resilience and flexibility of NIDS in dynamic threat settings.

articleTitle: Demystifying the Data: Leveraging Explainable AI for Real –Time Monitoring and Decision-Making in Vertical Hydroponics Farms
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Advances in Computing and Communications (ICACC)
abstract: A viable option for the productive and sustainable production of green vegetables is vertical hydroponic farms. However, in these regulated circumstances, making the best decisions and monitoring in real time might be difficult. This study investigates how Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) might be used to overcome these obstacles. We suggest a unique approach that combines multispectral imaging of the plants with sensor data from temperature, humidity, and nutrient levels. For real-time analysis, a machine learning model is then used, which has been trained on this combined dataset as well as previous data on disease outbreaks. Through the use of XAI approaches, the system is able to provide interpretable reasons for its conclusions in addition to identifying anomalies and possible illness signals. This enables farmers to make wise decisions for maximizing environmental conditions and obtain insightful knowledge on the health of their crops and prevent disease outbreaks. The purpose of this study is to show how successful XAI is in vertical hydroponic farming and how it can transform data-driven decision-making, real-time monitoring, and crop health and yield in these regulated settings.

articleTitle: Fast Iterative Filtering based approach for Seizure Detection in EEG Signals
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Advances in Computing and Communications (ICACC)
abstract: The increasing necessity for precise epilepsy diagnosis has amplified the demand for robust classification of EEG signals into seizure and non-seizure categories. In this study, we present a novel method employing the Fast Iterative Filtering (FIF) algorithm to tackle this critical challenge. FIF offers a computationally efficient approach by decomposing the EEG signals into Intrinsic Mode Functions (IMF’s). These IMF’s capture the inherent time-frequency characteristics of brain activity. Subsequently, informative statistical features are extracted from the decomposed IMF’s. These features effectively represent distinct characteristics of seizures and normal brain activity. By leveraging the feature extraction capabilities of FIF and the classification power of XGBoost, we aimed to achieve high-resolution and accurate seizure detection. It is shown that our proposed method can achieve a categorization accuracy of up to 95% for EEG datasets. This combination offers the potential of a highly accurate and practical tool for automated EEG seizure detection in clinical settings.

articleTitle: Skill Mount: Personalized Career Skills Development Using Machine Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Advances in Computing and Communications (ICACC)
abstract: In today’s rapidly changing job market, achieving career goals requires a strategic approach to skill development. Skill Mount is an intuitive web application designed to guide individuals through their career journeys, aiding in both planning and attainment of objectives through personalized technology-driven methods. Given the constant evolution of job roles and the competitive landscape, continuous skill enhancement is imperative for career advancement, making Skill Mount an indispensable tool. Serving as a personalized coach, it tailors daily skill acquisition plans, monitors progress, and suggests suitable job roles based on individual preferences. Leveraging artificial intelligence (AI), including Natural Language Processing (NLP) and Machine Learning (ML), Skill Mount analyzes user data to provide customized skill suggestions and job descriptions. The proposed system uses Recommendation Systems to propose relevant learning resources and utilizes an ensemble method (random forest algorithm) for job recommendations, As a result system acquired higher accuracy rates. With a focus on user experience (UX), Skill Mount ensures seamless interaction through its intuitive interface and automated features driven by AI. By simplifying the career journey and empowering individuals to adapt to the competitive job market, Skill Mount plays a pivotal role in facilitating career growth and success.

articleTitle: Antimicrobial Resistance Prediction using Neural Networks for Gonorrhea
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Advances in Computing and Communications (ICACC)
abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is an urgent and pressing global health challenge, and requires innovative methods for its prediction and management for better treatment plans for gonorrhea. Machine learning models are developed for predicting AMR in bacteria based on whole-genome sequence and clinical sample data. The ML methods extrapolate learned pattern occurrences in clinical samples and genomic data to infer potential resistance in a pathogen to a given antibiotic. The models used for the AMR prediction include Support Vector Machine (SVM), and neural networks like Convolution NN, Feedforward NN, and Recurrent NN. The review touches on the challenges of microbial genome diversity and the interpretability of machine learning models by visualizing data like average resistance level by country, the most resistant anitbiotic by country, and Spearman and Pearson correlation. The results have variable data quality, feature selection, and model optimization strategy parameters, such as hyperparameter tuning, which affect the accuracy in predicting AMR. Out of the ML models used SVM has the highest accuracy in terms of AMR prediction. It is the promise and use of ML-based AMR prediction systems in clinical practices to provide knowledge-guided personalized options to aid AR and improve the health outcomes of patients.
